---
title: "Capstone II — Master Problem Archive Guide, Judge Cross-Reference & Quarantined Template Ledger"
subtitle: "Complete Bijective Accounting of All 330 Accepted Non-Template Problems Across 57 Technique Families (T-1A-01–T-5B-08), Online Judge Lookup Index, and the 88 Quarantined Pure-Template Ledger (R-01–R-88)"
---

This second capstone serves as the master navigation and cross-reference index for the entire **Advanced Strings & Word Combinatorics (`strings/`)** problem corpus. Across our 10-wave research harvest (`445` raw problem entries consolidated into `418` unique canonical entries), every problem is partitioned **disjointly and bijectively** into two top-level classes:

$$
418 \text{ Canonical Entries} \;=\; \underbrace{248 \text{ Chapter Ladder Problems}}_{\text{Ch 01--Ch 30 (4-Tier Smooth Ladders)}} \;+\; \underbrace{52 \text{ Blind Checkpoint Problems}}_{\text{CP-I--CP-VII (Unspoiled Decoys)}} \;+\; \underbrace{30 \text{ Grandmaster Synthesis Problems}}_{\text{Capstone I (Syn-01--Syn-30)}} \;+\; \underbrace{88 \text{ Quarantined Pure Templates}}_{\text{Excluded per AGENTS.md (R-01--R-88)}}
$$

::: {.callout-tip}
## How to Use This Master Archive Without Spoiling Blind Practice

1. **Reverse-Lookup Without Spoilers (`Section 3`)**: When you encounter a problem on Codeforces, AtCoder, Luogu, UOJ, LOJ, QOJ, or in an Olympiad archive (`NOI`, `WC`, `CTSC`, `ZJOI`, `POI`, `ICPC WF`), look up its judge code in **Section 3** to see which **Part (`Part I`–`Part VII`)** it belongs to, and test yourself on the corresponding **Blind Checkpoint (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`)** before opening the chapter link.
2. **Audit Every Technique Family (`Section 2`)**: Use the **57-Technique Family Bijection Table** in Section 2 to locate the unique home chapter (`Ch 01`–`Ch 30`), prerequisites ($j < k$), and assigned problem ladder for every technique ID `T-1A-01` through `T-5B-08`.
3. **Understand Why Famous Template Problems Are Excluded (`Section 4`)**: Per our repository editorial policy (`AGENTS.md`), standard library verification tasks (Library Checker, Luogu `【模板】`, CSES/SPOJ bare template benchmarks) are excluded from all chapter ladders. **Section 4** documents all **88 Quarantined Pure-Template Problems (`R-01`–`R-88`)**, explains why each fails the structural-modeling bar, and links directly to the chapter that teaches its non-trivial combinatorial upgrade.
:::

## Editorial Quarantine Policy (`AGENTS.md` Compliance)

Per `AGENTS.md`, this textbook assumes the reader already possesses a tested competitive-programming library and **strictly excludes** practice problems whose primary task is copying, adapting, or validating a standard library routine. All **122 raw quarantined template entries** across the 10 research waves (`R-1A` through `R-5B`) are consolidated into the **88 canonical quarantine entries (`R-01`–`R-88`)** below. Each entry states why it is excluded and points to the textbook chapter teaching its structural invariant.

## 6. Master Structural Trap & Failure Mode Quick-Reference Index (`BP-01`–`BP-25`)

Every chapter in `strings/` pairs its algorithmic contract with an explicit **Broken Implementation / Counterexample Audit**. When debugging a Wrong Answer or Time Limit Exceeded on any of the 330 accepted problems, check your code against the 25 canonical stringology failure modes below:

| Trap Code | Failure Mode Name | What Breaks in the Naive Implementation | Canonical Fix & Home Chapter |
| :---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`BP-01`** | **Threshold-Boundary Fine–Wilf Assumption** | Assuming periods $p, q$ collapse to $\gcd(p, q)$ whenever $N \ge \max(p, q)$ instead of $N \ge p + q - \gcd(p, q)$. | Below $p+q-\gcd(p,q)$, exactly $p+q-N$ independent character orbits remain ([Ch 01](../chapters/ch01-fine-wilf-periodicity-orbits.qmd)). |
| **`BP-02`** | **Confusing `slink[u]` with `anc[u]` in Online KMP** | Using `slink[u]` (`diff[u] != diff[fail[u]]`) to skip mismatched borders in `CF 1286E` instead of `anc[u]` ($S[u+1] = S[\pi[u]+1]$). | `slink[u]` groups arithmetic progressions by period step; `anc[u]` groups by next-character equality ([Ch 02](../chapters/ch02-weak-periodicity-border-aps.qmd)). |
| **`BP-03`** | **0-1 vs. Unbounded Deque Push Order in `同余最短路`** | Pushing $D_{\text{old}}[v_t] - t\cdot d_k$ before updating $D[v_t]$ in `[WC2016] 论战捆竹竿`, missing multi-copy AP jumps. | Update $D[v_t]$ from the deque front **before** pushing $D[v_t] - t\cdot d_k$ for unbounded knapsack ([Ch 03](../chapters/ch03-border-modulo-shortest-path.qmd)). |
| **`BP-04`** | **Skipping Odd Prefixes in Interleaved PAM `slink` DP** | Updating `g[u]` only at even indices $2 \mid r$ in `CF 932G`, corrupting `g[fail[u]]` shift-overlap inheritance. | Update `g[u]` at **all** $r \in [1, N]$, and only gate the addition into `dp[r]` by $2 \mid r$ ([Ch 04](../chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd)). |
| **`BP-05`** | **Un-Swapped Parity Accumulators When `diff[u]` is Odd** | Inheriting `g_even[u] += g_even[fail[u]]` when $\text{diff}[u]$ is odd. | Stepping $r - d \to r$ adds $d$ to every length, flipping parity when $2 \nmid d$; swap `even` $\leftrightarrow$ `odd` ([Ch 04](../chapters/ch04-series-link-dp-kmp-pam.qmd)). |
| **`BP-06`** | **Interior RLE Split in Compressed Duval** | Splitting a unary run $c_t^{a_t}$ in the middle of a Lyndon factor of length $> 1$. | No Lyndon word of length $>1$ starts or ends strictly inside a run $c^a$; run Duval on whole RLE blocks ([Ch 05](../chapters/ch05-lyndon-factorization-duval-necklaces.qmd)). |
| **`BP-07`** | **Using $T=\varepsilon$ Shortest Border for Right-Extended Suffixes** | Assuming the minimum suffix of $S[l..r]$ is unique under right-extensions $+T_q$. | When $T_q \ne \varepsilon$, a longer bordered candidate in $\text{Cand}_{\min}(S[l..r])$ can beat its shortest border ([Ch 06](../chapters/ch06-significant-suffixes-substrings.qmd)). |
| **`BP-08`** | **The `bab` Trap: Negating $-\text{rk}_<$ for $\lambda_>$** | Computing the $>-$Lyndon array $\lambda_>$ by negating Suffix Array ranks $-\text{rk}_<[i]$ (`bab` gives $\text{rk}_<(\text{bab}) > \text{rk}_<(\text{b})$ yet $\text{bab} <_> \text{b}$!). | Build the Suffix Array on the **character-inverted string** $\overline{S}[t] = |\Sigma|+1-S[t]$ before running the stack ([Ch 07](../chapters/ch07-lyndon-arrays-cartesian-trees.qmd)). |
| **`BP-09`** | **Un-Deduplicated or Non-Primitive Run Roots** | Keeping multiple runs with the same $(l, r)$ or non-primitive period $k \cdot p$ during Lyndon-root seeding. | Group by $(l, r)$ and retain only the **minimum period $p$**, discarding $r - l + 1 < 2p$ ([Ch 08](../chapters/ch08-runs-theorem-squares-sweep.qmd)). |
| **`BP-10`** | **Trie-DFS $\Theta(V^2)$ Blowup & Zero-Length Clone in GSAM** | Building a GSAM via DFS on $\{\texttt{a}^k\texttt{b}\}$ ($\Theta(V^2)$) or allocating a new state when $\delta(p, c) = q$ already exists. | Traverse the Trie in **BFS order** and apply the 3-Case GSAM transition returning $q$ or `clone` directly ([Ch 09](../chapters/ch09-sam-duality-gsam-trie-bfs.qmd)). |
| **`BP-11`** | **Un-Clipped $[l, r]$ vs. $[l+L-1, r]$ in SAM $\text{endpos}$ Queries** | Querying $\text{endpos}(u) \cap [l, r] \ne \emptyset$ for a pattern of length $L$, allowing occurrences that start before $l$. | A substring of length $L$ lies inside $S[l..r]$ iff its right endpoint lies in $[l + L - 1, r]$ ([Ch 10](../chapters/ch10-sam-endpos-segtree-merge.qmd)). |
| **`BP-12`** | **Missing `access(q); splay(q);` Before LCT-SAM `clone`** | Copying `val[clone] = val[q]` during online LCT-SAM extension while lazy path-add tags still sit above $q$. | Always `access(q); splay(q);` before splitting $q \to \text{clone}$, and place $B_j$ before $A_i$ on length ties in `P5284` ([Ch 11](../chapters/ch11-dynamic-sam-lct-stratification.qmd)). |
| **`BP-13`** | **The `aba$` LMS Equality Trap in `SA-IS`** | Comparing adjacent LMS substrings by character equality alone without checking $L/S$ types. | Two LMS substrings are equal iff both their characters AND their $L/S$ types match at every offset ([Ch 12](../chapters/ch12-sais-induced-sorting-lcp.qmd)). |
| **`BP-14`** | **64-Bit Tag Overflow or Un-Maintained BST RMQ in Suffix BST** | Recomputing midpoint tags only at the rotated root or using polynomial hashing for $O(\log N)$ suffix comparisons. | Rebuild the entire $\alpha$-unbalanced Scapegoat subtree to refresh $[\ell, r]$ tags and maintain adjacent LCPs in the BST ([Ch 14](../chapters/ch14-cdawg-scdawg-suffix-balanced-trees.qmd)). |
| **`BP-15`** | **Treating Substring Borders as Center-Hereditary** | Attempting 1D binary search or unclipped RMQ for Range Longest Border (`[BJWC2018]`). | Borders are not hereditary; intersect dyadic IPM arithmetic progressions $P_m \cap Q_m$ at each scale $2^m$ ([Ch 15](../chapters/ch15-internal-pattern-matching-borders.qmd)). |
| **`BP-16`** | **Amortized PAM `fail` Walk on Version Trees / Deques** | Using standard while-loop `fail` walks on a branching version tree ($\Theta(N^2)$ star counterexample). | Use unamortized $O(1)$ `quick_link[u][c]` or $O(\log N)$ `slink` skipping, and push `fail[u]` lazily on Deque `pop` ([Ch 16](../chapters/ch16-deterministic-tree-deque-pam.qmd)). |
| **`BP-17`** | **Running 3 NTTs on an Involution $\pi^2 = \text{id}$** | Applying general permutation FFT when the compatibility relation $\pi$ is an involution (`CF 1334G`). | Collapse 2-cycles $\{c, \pi(c)\} \mapsto \min(c, \pi(c))$ and run KMP in $O(N+M)$ time ([Ch 18](../chapters/ch18-fft-wildcard-involution-matching.qmd)). |
| **`BP-18`** | **Un-Clipped Backward Offsets in `p-KMP` / `Order-KMP`** | Comparing raw `prev[i]` offsets without clipping links that point before the current window start $i - q$. | Always evaluate $\text{clip}(\text{prev}[i], q) = (\text{prev}[i] \le q \text{ ? } \text{prev}[i] : 0)$ ([Ch 20](../chapters/ch20-structural-isomorphism-weighted-strings.qmd)). |
| **`BP-19`** | **Crossing RLE Block Boundaries in Locally Consistent Parsing** | Pairing equal adjacent characters $cc$ during `PComp` when $c$ belongs to different lengths in two occurrences. | Always run `RComp` ($c^\ell \to (c, \ell)$) **before** `PComp`, and stop SLP LCE at the first block where $\ell_1 \ne \ell_2$ ([Ch 21](../chapters/ch21-locally-consistent-parsing-slp-attractors.qmd)). |
| **`BP-20`** | **Inverting Tropical $(\min,+)$ or Gap-2 ($\det = 0$) Matrices** | Attempting prefix-matrix inversion $\mathbf{u}_r^T \cdot \mathbf{v}_{l-1}$ on `CF 750E` (tropical semiring) or `ABC 214F` (gap-2 $\det M_c = 0$). | Prefix inversion works iff $\det M_c$ is a unit in a ring; use a Segment Tree when $\det = 0$ or in $(\min,+)$ ([Ch 22](../chapters/ch22-dasg-arch-simon-invertible-matrices.qmd)). |
| **`BP-21`** | **Un-Factored $x^{d_{\min}}$ in FPS $\ln/\exp$ & Un-Shifted $D_0(x)^{K+1}$** | Calling $\ln D_1(x)$ when $[x^0]D_1(x) = 0$, or running Bostan–Mori on $D_0(x)^{K+1}$ at $|P|=10^5, n=10^{18}$. | Factor out $x^{d_{\min}}$ before `ln`/`exp`, and substitute $t = 1 + u$ so the denominator collapses to $(1-\sigma x)^{j+1}$ ([Ch 24](../chapters/ch24-goulden-jackson-moment-shift-fps.qmd)). |
| **`BP-22`** | **Transposed $\Omega_{P_i, P_j}$ in Conway Pattern Races** | Computing $\Omega_{P_j, P_i}$ (gambler $P_i$ on terminal $P_j$) instead of $\Omega_{P_i, P_j}$ (suffix of winner $P_i$ = prefix of gambler $P_j$). | Row $j$'s equation tests suffixes of winner $P_i$ against prefixes of gambler $P_j$; multiply by $\mathbb{P}(P_j)$ for zero division ([Ch 25](../chapters/ch25-martingale-pgfs-automaton-dp-of-dp.qmd)). |
| **`BP-23`** | **The $N=4$ Self-Loop Bug (`rx == ry, rel == 1`) in Signed DSU** | Ignoring a merge `unite(k, x, y, 1)` when `rx == ry`, losing the constraint that block $B_k(rx)$ is a self-palindrome! | Maintain `is_pal[k][rx] = 1` and push $B_{k-1}(r) = B_{k-1}(r+2^{k-1})^R$ down to level $k-1$ ([Ch 26](../chapters/ch26-word-equations-signed-parallel-dsu.qmd)). |
| **`BP-24`** | **Dividing by $\prod_{u,v} A(u,v)!$ Instead of $\prod_{u,c} \text{count}(u,c)!$ in AC-BEST** | Treating parallel transitions $u \xrightarrow{c_1} v$ and $u \xrightarrow{c_2} v$ ($c_1 \ne c_2$) as indistinguishable edges in `UOJ #607`. | Divide by $\prod_{u \in V, c \in \Sigma} \text{count}(u, c)!$ because distinct character labels produce distinct strings ([Ch 28](../chapters/ch28-debruijn-best-bwt-wheeler-rlbwt.qmd)). |
| **`BP-25`** | **Kasai's Algorithm on Trees & Un-Indexed $SL_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ Dyck Matrices** | Running Kasai's $h[\text{rk}[u]] \ge h[\text{rk}[\text{parent}(u)]] - 1$ on trees, or mapping $\texttt{)} \mapsto M_{\texttt{(}}^{-1}$ without height indexing (`(( )( ))` bug). | Use binary lifting for Tree LCP; index Dyck generators by balance height $M_{(c, \text{bal}[i])}$ + range-min balance ([Ch 29](../chapters/ch29-tree-strings-stack-trie-sl2-hashing.qmd)). |

## 7. Zero-Forward-Reference Prerequisite DAG & Corpus Verification Checklist

All **330 accepted non-template problems** obey a strict **Zero-Forward-Reference Invariant**: if a problem located in Chapter $X$ requires a secondary tool from Chapter $Y$, then $Y < X$ in the textbook sequence (`Ch 01`–`Ch 30`). Any problem that fuses paradigms across parts where $Y > X$ relative to its primary paradigm is assigned to its highest-index constituent chapter, its part's blind checkpoint (`CP-I`–`CP-VII`), or the **[Grandmaster Multi-Chapter Synthesis Capstone (`Syn-01`–`Syn-30`)](synthesis.qmd)**.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P1["Part I (Ch 01–04)<br/>Periodicity, Orbits & slink"] --> P2["Part II (Ch 05–08)<br/>Lyndon, Candidates & Runs"]
  P1 --> P3["Part III (Ch 09–14)<br/>SAM, SA-IS, Dominants & CDAWG"]
  P2 --> P3
  P1 --> P4["Part IV (Ch 15–17)<br/>IPM, Deque PAM & Range Palindromes"]
  P3 --> P4
  P3 --> P5["Part V (Ch 18–21)<br/>FFT, Isomorphism & LCP-SLP"]
  P1 --> P6["Part VI (Ch 22–25)<br/>DASG, Seaweeds, GJ & DP套DP"]
  P3 --> P6
  P2 --> P7["Part VII (Ch 26–30)<br/>Equations, Trees, BWT & Morphic"]
  P4 --> P7
  P5 --> P7
  P6 --> P7
  P7 --> SYN["Synthesis Capstone<br/>(Syn-01 – Syn-30)"]
```
